decisions.situation: Rank gap: an enemy Rank 3 blocks the path to a needed resource; his force is Rank 2 peak.
decisions.objective: Get the resource without direct combat.
known_facts: rank gap makes combat near-suicidal
the enemy patrols on schedule
the resource is guarded, not carried
options: wait for a third-party raid to stretch the patrol, then enter through the secondary route
decisions.selected_action: wait for a third-party raid to stretch the patrol, then enter through the secondary route
result: resource taken; no engagement
lesson: a stronger opponent is a scheduling problem, not a combat problem

decisions.situation: His primeval essence reserve is low and regeneration is slow; a fight may come within days.
decisions.objective: Allocate the limited essence between readiness and progress.
known_facts: full readiness stalls cultivation
full progress leaves him vulnerable
threat timing is probabilistic
options: hold full reserve until threat passes
tiered reserve: minimum combat threshold maintained, surplus invested, sensors positioned to buy reaction time
decisions.selected_action: tiered reserve: minimum combat threshold maintained, surplus invested, sensors positioned to buy reaction time
result: progress continued at bounded risk
lesson: treat essence like working capital: threshold + investable surplus

decisions.situation: A Gu in his set has feeding requirements that will soon exceed his production.
decisions.objective: Resolve the feeding gap before it becomes a crisis.
known_facts: starved Gu degrade or turn hostile
production can be raised (inputs), lowered (downgrade Gu), or outsourced (feeding contracts)
each route has different exposure
unknowns: input price trend in the region
options: secure a medium-term input contract while adjusting the Gu set composition
decisions.selected_action: secure a medium-term input contract while adjusting the Gu set composition
result: feeding secured; set optimized for production reality
lesson: feed the system or shrink the system; never let it starve slowly

decisions.situation: A rare inheritance clue surfaces at an auction embedded in an unrelated lot.
decisions.objective: Acquire the clue without signaling its value.
known_facts: clue value is verifiable only with his knowledge
bidding interest on the lot would reprice it
auction houses sell bidder lists
unknowns: whether the seller knows the lot's content
options: bribe auction staff for a side sale
win the lot through a proxy with a history of odd purchases
decisions.selected_action: win the lot through a proxy with a history of odd purchases
result: clue acquired inside noise
lesson: mispriced information is the highest-margin trade
buy the container, not the content

decisions.situation: A stronger cultivator offers 'protection' in exchange for a periodic cut — a protection racket with honorable framing.
decisions.objective: Avoid the cut without open defiance.
known_facts: open defiance invites immediate enforcement
payment establishes a ratchet
the protector's reputation depends on smooth extraction
options: join a rival's umbrella or relocate operations so that the protector's marginal enforcement cost exceeds the cut's value
decisions.selected_action: join a rival's umbrella or relocate operations so that the protector's marginal enforcement cost exceeds the cut's value
result: racket outcompeted by structure, not by fight
lesson: outprice the extortion; make enforcement unprofitable

decisions.situation: Two mentors offer instruction: one prestigious and slow, one obscure and fast with a dark reputation.
decisions.objective: Choose instruction by path value, not prestige.
known_facts: prestige brings scrutiny and slow curriculum
the obscure route compresses years but marks its graduates
his objective is personal, not institutional
options: take the obscure route with pre-agreed exit terms and information safeguards
decisions.selected_action: take the obscure route with pre-agreed exit terms and information safeguards
result: compressed capability at controlled tail risk
lesson: buy skills on the fast path; pre-price the stigma
prestige is a costume worn by curricula

decisions.situation: A hostile formation locks the area; brute-force breaking alerts its owner.
decisions.objective: Exit the formation's trap without the alert.
known_facts: formations have maintenance rhythms and blind spots
the owner expects trapped prey to thrash
time inside is against him
options: probe for the rhythm, spoof a failure state, walk out through the maintenance blind spot
decisions.selected_action: probe for the rhythm, spoof a failure state, walk out through the maintenance blind spot
result: exit without alert
lesson: systems have rhythms; the rhythm is the door
never thrash in a trap; audit it

decisions.situation: A market rumor says a faction will ban export of a key input next month.
decisions.objective: Position before confirmation without betting everything.
known_facts: rumors have higher-than-chance accuracy when self-serving leaks exist
the ban would spike prices sharply
full conviction position is ruin-prone if the rumor is false
unknowns: whether the rumor is planted to bait hoarders
options: stage accumulation in tranches as independent confirmations arrive, with a pre-set exit if disconfirmed
decisions.selected_action: stage accumulation in tranches as independent confirmations arrive, with a pre-set exit if disconfirmed
result: meaningful position at controlled ruin exposure
lesson: act on probabilistic information in tranches, never in conviction
set the disconfirmation exit before entering

decisions.situation: A subordinate completed a mission with excessive collateral damage that draws enforcement attention.
decisions.objective: Correct the tool without breaking it.
known_facts: the tool's aggression has value elsewhere
enforcement attention is the current binding cost
harsh correction now prevents worse later
options: reprice: fine the damage against his pay, reassign to contexts where aggression is priced high, and pair him with a restraining partner
decisions.selected_action: reprice: fine the damage against his pay, reassign to contexts where aggression is priced high, and pair him with a restraining partner
result: tool retained; damage priced into his incentives
lesson: behavior follows pricing; anger is not a policy
match tools to markets that value their defects

decisions.situation: An enemy holds a family member of a useful ally as leverage against the ally's loyalty to him.
decisions.objective: Keep the ally's loyalty economically.
known_facts: the enemy's leverage is hostage-based
rescue operations are expensive and risky
the ally's loyalty is genuine but held hostage
options: match the enemy's leverage with his own threats
fund and enable a rescue while restructuring the ally's role so that hostage-coercion loses value
decisions.selected_action: fund and enable a rescue while restructuring the ally's role so that hostage-coercion loses value
result: hostage lever broken; loyalty retained by choice plus incentive
lesson: break hostage levers structurally, not just tactically
loyalty under coercion is rented by the enemy until the rent is removed

decisions.situation: He notices his own decision quality degrading under sustained sleepless operation during a crisis.
decisions.objective: Budget cognition like any resource.
known_facts: errors cluster when exhausted
opponents exploit predictable fatigue windows
delegation can carry routine load
options: institute rotation and checklists, reserve personal cognition for irreversible decisions only, and rest on a schedule
decisions.selected_action: institute rotation and checklists, reserve personal cognition for irreversible decisions only, and rest on a schedule
result: error rate contained; crisis managed across days
lesson: cognition is the scarcest resource; never spend it on reversible choices
rest is a tactical asset, scheduled like any other

decisions.situation: Opportunity to sell a 'cursed' item he knows is not cursed to a superstitious buyer at a massive discount-plus story.
decisions.objective: Decide whether to run the deception.
known_facts: the buyer's superstition is verifiable
the sale is one-shot and reputation-irrelevant in that market
similar buyers exist elsewhere
unknowns: whether the buyer resells and claims fraud loudly
options: sell honestly but with the 'cursed' discount story as an option he can deploy later in a distress liquidity event
decisions.selected_action: sell honestly but with the 'cursed' discount story as an option he can deploy later in a distress liquidity event
result: clean reputation kept; option banked
lesson: deceptions burn options; spend them only at distress prices
keep the lie as inventory

decisions.situation: A faction offers to buy his entire production output long-term at good fixed prices.
decisions.objective: Price the information leakage of exclusive output.
known_facts: exclusive output reveals his capability curve precisely
fixed prices hedge his downside
single-buyer dependency is a leash
options: accept a capped share (e.g. 40%) with market-rate escape clauses and mixed buyers
decisions.selected_action: accept a capped share (e.g. 40%) with market-rate escape clauses and mixed buyers
result: hedge secured; capability curve obfuscated
lesson: never sell 100% of anything to one buyer
output data is strategic data

decisions.situation: He can license his refinement method to a guild for recurring royalties instead of selling goods.
decisions.objective: Compare method-sale vs product-sale economics.
known_facts: methods replicate and leak
royalties require enforcement against infringement
product sales keep the method secret and the margin whole
options: keep the method, expand own production
license an obsolete version of the method while keeping the current one
decisions.selected_action: license an obsolete version of the method while keeping the current one
result: royalty stream from a decoy; real edge retained
lesson: sell the previous version of anything replicable
methods are compounding assets; ration their exposure

decisions.situation: A buyer defaults on a large delivery after receiving goods, citing quality disputes in bad faith.
decisions.objective: Recover value without a public war.
known_facts: litigation reveals his reach and priorities
the buyer fears his other suppliers more than him
goods are already integrated and hard to reclaim
options: orchestrate a coordinated credit tightening by his other suppliers, then buy the buyer's distressed obligations cheaply
decisions.selected_action: orchestrate a coordinated credit tightening by his other suppliers, then buy the buyer's distressed obligations cheaply
result: debt recovered at discount via structure
lesson: bad-faith default is a liquidity problem; attack the liquidity
let the market squeeze what the sword cannot

decisions.situation: After betrayal by a collaborator mid-venture, the venture is at a decision point and the collaborator still holds needed skills.
decisions.objective: Continue the venture with betrayed-but-bounded cooperation.
known_facts: the collaborator's betrayal was self-interested, not personal
replacement cost exceeds supervision cost
the venture's remaining value is real
unknowns: whether the collaborator already sold more information
options: continue with constrained access, milestone payments, verification gates, and a replacement in training
decisions.selected_action: continue with constrained access, milestone payments, verification gates, and a replacement in training
result: venture completed; dependency on the traitor reduced each phase
lesson: betrayal reprices the contract, not the venture
replace trust with structure, and prepare the replacement

decisions.situation: Long-horizon path requires a decade of quiet accumulation while rivals burn resources in an open war they started.
decisions.objective: Stay out, accumulate, and harvest the aftermath.
known_facts: the war consumes both sides' stockpiles
post-war demand spikes across categories
neutrality is credible only with distance and smallness
unknowns: whether either side will coerce neutrals late-war
options: stay visible-neutral in the war zone
operate quietly from adjacent markets, stockpile for post-war demand, and enter reconstruction when both sides are exhausted
decisions.selected_action: operate quietly from adjacent markets, stockpile for post-war demand, and enter reconstruction when both sides are exhausted
decisions.cost: foregone war profits; patience across years
result: reconstruction windfall with intact capital
lesson: wars are other people's resource destruction
the patient book wins the fighting book's money

decisions.situation: He must choose his cultivation path specialization with decade-scale consequences.
decisions.objective: Pick the path by compounding logic, not by fashion or immediate power.
known_facts: paths differ in resource appetite, scalability, and scarcity
fashionable paths have crowded resources and priced teachers
his prior-life knowledge gives unusual path insight
unknowns: which legacy assets will surface later
options: the path whose bottleneck resources he can control or produce, aligned with legacy knowledge
decisions.selected_action: the path whose bottleneck resources he can control or produce, aligned with legacy knowledge
decisions.cost: scarcity of teachers; slower early progress
result: path compounding without resource hostage-taking
lesson: specialize where you own the bottleneck
fashion is a tax on the impatient

decisions.situation: An enemy coalition forms specifically against him after a series of successes.
decisions.objective: Break the coalition's glue.
known_facts: coalitions form on fear and share of spoils promises
members have divergent interests and different threat perceptions
his recent visibility created the glue
unknowns: which member is the coalition's spine
options: reduce perceived threat, reprice spoils for the spine member, and give the weakest member a better private deal
decisions.selected_action: reduce perceived threat, reprice spoils for the spine member, and give the weakest member a better private deal
result: coalition frays into bilateral deals he controls
lesson: coalitions are priced structures, not friendships
defeat the glue, not the members

decisions.situation: A once-in-an-era opportunity (legacy/venue) opens far from his base while his base operations need supervision.
decisions.objective: Take the opportunity without losing the base.
known_facts: the opportunity is transformative
base operations can run unsupervised for a bounded period at reduced efficiency
absence invites probing at the base
options: harden the base, delegate with audit, leave a proxy presence, and go with a hard return-deadline
decisions.selected_action: harden the base, delegate with audit, leave a proxy presence, and go with a hard return-deadline
result: opportunity pursued; base survived on structure
lesson: transformative windows justify travel; structure pays for absence
hard deadlines prevent opportunity creep

decisions.situation: A clever multi-layer deception of his was undone because a subordinate improvised an extra layer he had not coordinated.
decisions.objective: Fix the coordination failure pattern.
known_facts: uncoordinated improvisation contradicted the plan
the target's verification caught the seam
the subordinate acted with good intent
unknowns: whether the seam exposed the whole architecture
options: abandon layered deceptions as too fragile
simplify deception architectures and pre-brief seams so every actor knows the same false picture
decisions.selected_action: simplify deception architectures and pre-brief seams so every actor knows the same false picture
result: later deceptions held under target verification
lesson: every extra layer multiplies seam risk
the false picture must be one picture

decisions.situation: He dismissed a minor rival as irrelevant; the rival later sabotaged a critical supply line at the worst moment.
decisions.objective: Correct the threat-assessment model.
known_facts: the rival's motive was durable humiliation resentment
minor players can hold critical-path positions
his dismissal was emotional shorthand, not analysis
unknowns: which other 'irrelevant' parties sit on critical paths
options: map all critical paths against all resentments (not just powerful actors) and neutralize or indemnify the overlaps
decisions.selected_action: map all critical paths against all resentments (not just powerful actors) and neutralize or indemnify the overlaps
result: critical paths de-risked from small actors
lesson: threat assessment is positional, not status-based
humiliation creates enemies with nothing to lose

decisions.situation: A truce he signed was exploited by the enemy to reposition forces legally under its terms.
decisions.objective: Repair the truce model.
known_facts: the enemy read the terms better
his own team drafted hastily under pressure
repositioning now advantages the enemy
unknowns: which clauses the enemy targets next
options: honor it to the letter and lose
invoke review clauses, trade concessions for amendments, and institute adversarial legal review before signing anything
decisions.selected_action: invoke review clauses, trade concessions for amendments, and institute adversarial legal review before signing anything
result: truce restructured; review discipline institutionalized
lesson: contracts are battlefield maps drawn in advance
pay lawyers before you pay defeats

decisions.situation: He trusted a translation of an ancient text (secondary source) that turned out to be corrupted, misleading a whole operation.
decisions.objective: Correct the epistemic pipeline.
known_facts: secondary sources embed errors at copy time
the operation followed the corrupted text faithfully
originals exist in restricted collections
unknowns: which other conclusions rest on the same source
options: proceed; one error is bad luck
build a source-registry discipline: originals preferred, translations flagged, cross-readings required for critical parameters
decisions.selected_action: build a source-registry discipline: originals preferred, translations flagged, cross-readings required for critical parameters
result: epistemic quality hardened; later text-based operations reliable
lesson: citation discipline is operational security for the mind
never let one copy decide a decade

decisions.situation: An ally interpreted his calculated generosity as genuine friendship and began acting on emotional claims (favors, exceptions).
decisions.objective: Recalibrate the ally's model of the relationship without cruelty.
known_facts: generosity was priced into a strategy
the ally's model updated on evidence
unbounded claims will grow
options: recalibrate openly: convert the relationship to explicit terms with priced favors and a stated boundary
decisions.selected_action: recalibrate openly: convert the relationship to explicit terms with priced favors and a stated boundary
result: claims bounded; relationship honest and stable
lesson: price generosity at issuance or it will be repriced by the receiver
clear terms are kinder than accumulating resentment

decisions.situation: A grand plan collapsed because a single assumed constant (a river's seasonal level) changed after decades of stability.
decisions.objective: Fix the assumption inventory.
known_facts: constants are assumptions with long half-lives
climate/geology/politics all shift slowly
the plan failed at execution, not design
options: rebuild the same plan with current data
institutionalize an assumption registry with periodic re-verification and plan-version branches for shifts
decisions.selected_action: institutionalize an assumption registry with periodic re-verification and plan-version branches for shifts
result: plans gained shock absorption
lesson: list your assumptions or they will list your failures
branch plans before reality branches for you

decisions.situation: His current mask's community expects periodic public generosity; the requests grow with his displayed wealth.
decisions.objective: Sustain the mask at bounded cost.
known_facts: visibility of wealth sets the expectation base
refusals are remembered longer than gifts
anonymized giving dampens expectations
unknowns: who measures his wealth and how
options: cap visible wealth display, shift giving to anonymized channels, and endow a named structure (school/shrine) that absorbs all requests into one bounded institution
decisions.selected_action: cap visible wealth display, shift giving to anonymized channels, and endow a named structure (school/shrine) that absorbs all requests into one bounded institution
result: expectations institutionalized and capped
lesson: institutions cap infinite asks
manage the display of wealth, not just the wealth

decisions.situation: A righteous sect publicly names him (masked) as an example of virtue and requests he teach juniors.
decisions.objective: Convert the honor into leverage without teaching anything real.
known_facts: teaching raises standing and cements the mask
juniors repeat everything to elders
his real methods must not transfer
unknowns: the sect's real motive (honor or audit)
options: teach a curated orthodoxy: correct-but-generic methods, heavy on virtue theory, light on technique — becoming beloved for wisdom while transferring nothing sharp
decisions.selected_action: teach a curated orthodoxy: correct-but-generic methods, heavy on virtue theory, light on technique — becoming beloved for wisdom while transferring nothing sharp
decisions.cost: time; platitude reputation risk among experts
result: mask cemented; nothing weaponizable transferred
lesson: teach the shoulder, never the blade
wisdom reputation is cheap armor

decisions.situation: A rich heir offers partnership based on admiring his (masked) persona's 'honest success'.
decisions.objective: Use the heir's capital without inheriting his foolery.
known_facts: the heir's capital is real
his admiration makes him pliable
his family monitors the capital
options: accept as a managed venture: his honest persona takes stewardship, capital is tranched against milestones, family gets transparent books
decisions.selected_action: accept as a managed venture: his honest persona takes stewardship, capital is tranched against milestones, family gets transparent books
result: capital employed; family's trust reinforced the mask
lesson: admiration is capital's soft door
transparency for the family, stewardship for the heir

decisions.situation: A demon-hunting patrol requests his (masked righteous) help tracking 'a demon' who is, in fact, an associate of his.
decisions.objective: Degrade the hunt without direct sabotage.
known_facts: participation is expected of righteous locals
the associate's trail is partially real
patrols depend on local guides
unknowns: whether the patrol already holds hard evidence
options: guide enthusiastically but ineptly: honest effort, poor instincts, dead-end trails, and a 'the demon likely fled the region' conclusion
decisions.selected_action: guide enthusiastically but ineptly: honest effort, poor instincts, dead-end trails, and a 'the demon likely fled the region' conclusion
result: hunt dissolved; associate warned via indirect channel
lesson: sabotage through sincere incompetence is unfalsifiable
be the guide who tries his best

decisions.situation: His mask persona's fabricated backstory contains a detail an educated listener finds chronologically impossible.
decisions.objective: Repair the backstory in real time.
known_facts: the listener is testing, not accusing
a repair that fights the detail deepens the hole
concession on trivia builds credibility
unknowns: what else the listener has checked
options: concede warmly ('my grandfather's telling was muddled — you know records better than I'), then redirect to the listener's expertise
decisions.selected_action: concede warmly ('my grandfather's telling was muddled — you know records better than I'), then redirect to the listener's expertise
result: test passed; listener flattered; story patched
lesson: trivia is cheap; concession on trivia is expensive armor
flattery is a legitimate redirect
